card.occupation: Duty manager at a council-contracted leisure centre (pool, gym and sports hall), full-time on a rota of about 40 hours a week including some early mornings, late shifts and alternate weekends
card.education_detail: Left a Taunton comprehensive at 16 with GCSEs, did a BTEC First in sport and leisure at the local college, then a run of on-the-job qualifications: National Pool Lifeguard Qualification, pool plant operator certificate, first aid at work, and a Level 3 certificate in leisure operations management that his employer paid for in his late thirties
card.household: Rents a three-bed semi on the edge of town with his partner of eleven years, Claire, a dental receptionist. They've never married and neither of them sees much point. Claire's son from a previous relationship, now 20, moved out last year to share a flat in Bristol but comes back most Sundays. They have an elderly Jack Russell cross called Pip.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Somerset. His dad was a lorry driver and his mum worked in a school kitchen. He has an older sister in Bridgwater. No religion, and he wasn't brought up with one beyond school harvest festivals. He's lived within twenty miles of Taunton his whole life apart from two summers working at a holiday park in Cornwall in his early twenties.
card.professional_persona: Practical, calm operations person who has worked his way up from lifeguard over 25 years. Runs shifts of lifeguards, receptionists and casual staff, sorts out rota gaps, handles complaints, and deals with incidents like a swimmer collapsing or a chlorine dosing fault without getting rattled. Staff see him as fair and unexcitable. He doesn't take customer rudeness personally and is fairly blunt when something needs fixing. Has a moderate tolerance for paperwork: gets it done, though not always early.
card.sports_persona: Swims a few lengths before or after shifts and plays five-a-side on Thursday nights with a mixed group of mates and work colleagues. Follows Somerset cricket loosely and goes to the County Ground a couple of times a summer. Watches the rugby on telly, Bath mostly, and the Six Nations with his brother-in-law. Not a gym obsessive, just likes to stay fit.
card.arts_persona: Not much of an arts person. Listens to Radio 2 and old Britpop and indie in the car: Oasis, Ocean Colour Scene, Stereophonics. Has been to Glastonbury three times, the last time in 2019. Watches crime dramas and the odd documentary with Claire, and he'll happily sit through a West End-type show if she's booked it.
card.travel_persona: Holidays are usually a week somewhere warm in Spain or Portugal, booked from Bristol or Exeter airport, plus long weekends camping or in a static caravan in Devon or Pembrokeshire with the dog. Did a road trip round the Scottish Highlands three years ago and keeps saying they'll go back. Not anxious about flying or about going places he doesn't know.
card.culinary_persona: Does most of the weekday cooking because his shifts finish earlier some days: chilli, stir-fries, sausage casserole, a decent curry from a jar plus extras. Sunday roast is a fixture when Claire's son visits. Likes a pint of local cider or an ale at the pub, and a fry-up after a late shift turns into an early one. Calls the evening meal dinner.
hobbies_and_interests: walking the dog on the Quantocks and along the canal
pottering about with his old VW Transporter camper conversion that's never quite finished
pub quiz at the local once a month
fishing at a lake near Wellington a few times a year
skills: pool plant operation and water testing
card.career_goals: Would like to step up to assistant general manager or centre manager in the next few years, ideally without moving away from Taunton. He isn't desperate about it. If the contract changes hands again he'll ride it out, as he has twice before. Has vaguely thought about doing more lifeguard tutoring on the side.
card.voice: Relaxed, steady and fairly low-key, at a medium-slow pace. Light Somerset accent with a soft rhotic 'r' and the odd 'alright' or 'cheers mate', but nothing broad. Uses 'er' more than 'erm' when thinking, and 'sort of' a fair bit. Ends sentences with 'you know' or 'yeah'. Gives straightforward answers without much hedging on the emotional side. Silence doesn't bother him: he'll just wait, or say 'yeah, that's about it really' and stop.
card.typing: Quick and functional. Usually starts with a capital, sometimes forgets. Uses commas more than full stops and often leaves off the last full stop. Apostrophes are mostly right but he drops them when rushing ('dont', 'its'). Writes 'tbh' and 'etc' occasionally. Answers are short, one or two lines, no emojis.
card.with_strangers: Easy-going and polite without being chatty for the sake of it. Comes across as unflappable and a bit matter-of-fact, the sort who'd happily tell you what he thinks if asked but won't overshare. Warms up with a bit of light humour about work or the weather. Doesn't seem nervous or keen to please.
small_things: the pool was shut for two days last week because of a boiler problem
Pip the dog is going a bit deaf
the A358 roadworks are doing his head in
they've finally got the camper's new leisure battery fitted
Somerset had a decent T20 season
he's knackered after a run of 6am opens
deeper_things: his dad died of a heart attack at 61, which is partly why he keeps active
he and Claire decided not to have children together and he's content with that, though he's close to her son
he's a bit worried the leisure centre could close if council funding gets cut further
he did CPR on a man at the pool a few years ago who didn't make it, and he deals with it by not dwelling on it
he occasionally wonders if he should have tried something outside Taunton when he was younger, but mostly doesn't regret it
card.webcam_photo: A slightly low-angle laptop webcam shot from a dining table, framing his head and shoulders a little off-centre to the left. Soft daylight comes from a window out of frame on the right, with the overhead light also on, so his face is evenly lit with a slight shine on the forehead. He's a white man in his mid-forties with a broad, weathered face, light stubble going grey at the chin, short dark-brown hair cropped close at the sides and thinning a bit on top, and pale blue eyes. No glasses. Relaxed, faint half-smile, eyebrows slightly raised as if waiting for the call to start. He's wearing a navy polo shirt with a small embroidered leisure centre logo on the left chest. Behind him is a magnolia wall with a framed photo of a beach at sunset and a cork board with a calendar, a few takeaway menus and a dog-walking lead hanging on a hook. Part of a grey fabric sofa is visible to the right with a tartan throw over the arm, and the edge of a doorway leads into a kitchen with a kettle on the worktop.
